blanks.sentence: Gross National Happiness links development with the _____ of nature and culture.
Bhutan tries to follow a model of sustainable and _____.
For a long time, Bhutan had limited contact with the _____.
The King wanted people to gain the advantages of _____ without harming traditions.
Modernisation was expected to protect culture, the environment and Bhutan’s strong _____.
Citizens’ happiness became the country’s central _____.
Some workers left Bhutan to look for _____ and opportunities abroad.
The Mindfulness City is planned to run on _____.
The city aims to bring back _____ who have gained experience overseas.
Workers may apply abilities developed overseas through _____.

multipleChoice.question: What makes Bhutan’s approach to national progress different from a purely economic model?
options: It rejects modern development completely.
It places environmental and cultural goals above unrestricted growth.
It measures success only through religious practice.
It depends mainly on international tourism.

multipleChoice.question: What tension was the King trying to manage?
options: Attracting tourists while removing television.
Increasing exports while reducing local jobs.
Replacing Buddhist traditions with new policies.
Opening up to technology while protecting cultural life.

multipleChoice.question: Why is Bhutan presented as having a particularly well-preserved culture?
options: It avoided colonisation and kept its traditions largely undamaged.
It banned outside experts from influencing government policy.
It developed faster than most other Asian countries.
It used tourism to rebuild lost cultural practices.

multipleChoice.question: What does the phrase “took centre stage” suggest in this context?
options: It became a public performance for citizens.
It was discussed only in cultural events.
It became the main focus of government thinking.
It was treated as less urgent than growth.

multipleChoice.question: What problem did Bhutan face despite global admiration for its happiness policy?
options: Foreign workers were replacing local communities.
Skilled citizens were leaving for better opportunities abroad.
The government stopped investing in education.
Tourists were discouraged by environmental rules.

multipleChoice.question: How is The Mindfulness City characterised?
options: A conventional industrial zone for foreign investors.
A heritage district designed mainly for tourists.
A temporary employment scheme outside Bhutan.
A new city guided by spiritual and environmental values.

multipleChoice.question: Why is the project linked to Bhutan’s brain drain?
options: It is intended to draw back people who have left the country.
It will prevent all young people from studying overseas.
It replaces local workers with foreign experts.
It mainly records why citizens choose to migrate.

multipleChoice.question: What value might returning migrants bring to The Mindfulness City?
options: They can help Bhutan depend less on environmental policies.
They can introduce colonisation-era traditions.
They can use skills acquired from overseas work.
They can make the city separate from local society.

multipleChoice.question: What does “upskilling” refer to in this discussion?
options: Moving trained workers permanently overseas.
Creating higher salaries without extra training.
Selecting only foreign experts for a project.
Improving workers’ abilities through training.

multipleChoice.question: What broader conclusion is drawn about Bhutan’s model?
options: It attempts to combine economic development with citizens’ wellbeing.
It proves economic growth is unnecessary for happiness.
It shows migration can be solved without policy action.
It argues that technology is harmful in every country.
